message.content:
The **C♯ major** scale consists of the following eight notes (the octave repeats the first note):

| Scale Degree | Note |
|--------------|------|
| 1 (tonic)    | C♯   |
| 2 (supertonic) | D♯ |
| 3 (mediant) | E♯ (which is enharmonically equivalent to F) |
| 4 (subdominant) | F♯ |
| 5 (dominant) | G♯ |
| 6 (submediant) | A♯ |
| 7 (leading tone) | B♯ (enharmonically equivalent to C) |
| 8 (octave) | C♯ |

So the full C♯ major scale is:

**C♯ – D♯ – E♯ – F♯ – G♯ – A♯ – B♯ – C♯**

(If you prefer to use the enharmonic equivalents, it can also be written as: C♯ – D♯ – F – F♯ – G♯ – A♯ – C – C♯.)
message.reasoning: User asks: "What is the musical scale associated with C sharp major?" They want the notes of the C# major scale. We can answer: C#, D#, E#, F#, G#, A#, B#, C#. But E# is F, B# is C. So the scale: C#, D#, E#, F#, G#, A#, B#, C#. Or list as C#, D#, E#, F#, G#, A#, B#, C#. Provide explanation. No function needed.
